Each ticket has one durable authoritative record; the default carrier is
one markdown file.

A multi-build-tenant work item is one admitted upstream work item with more

`chore`. A project may add more; the default set should be enough for
most cases

concepts.label: Ticket type

concepts.definition: The execution or migration discipline governing a ticket, orthogonal to type. Its minimum common set is ordinary and implementation_migration; feature, bug, spike and chore can each carry either category.

Ticket category is orthogonal to ticket type: type answers what kind of
work record this is; category answers what execution or migration
discipline governs the ticket (P3, P1; rc.2 #ticket-category). The minimum

concepts.definition: A governed replacement of one implementation truth path by another across producers, consumers, projections and proof surfaces. Examples include replacing a tracker or read-model family with one authoritative carrier, introducing a public interface requiring migration of every producer and consumer before closure, and removing a bridge or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.

grounding.quote:
`implementation_migration` is
used when the ticket is not "change code until tests pass" but a governed
replacement of one implementation truth path with another across producers,
consumers, projections and proof surfaces: a bug ticket that replaces an old
tracker or read-model family with one new authoritative carrier; a feature
ticket that introduces a new public interface and requires every producer
and consumer to migrate before closure; a refactor ticket that removes a
bridge path or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.

concepts.label: Implementation migration ticket

concepts.definition: The intake-triage declaration of where a change lawfully re-enters the constitutional chain, using SPEC_METHOD §4 classes. work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully

declared by intake triage, using the classes of

concepts.label: Change class

The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the
sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`
values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map
to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under

`backlog`

current execution focus; `active` is the current bounded execution set;
`completed` is closed work retained as history.

concepts.label: Ticket states and lanes

Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
work authority, then select the first matching row below. For work inside
an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it
is the current run

concepts.definition: F13 is the source's work-carrier family: selection of the record carrying work, its permitted claims and closure. Instance premises concern lifetimes, several apparent state surfaces, several build tenants, truth-path migrations and variation among files, trackers and services. Cited standing is P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 with the non-reacquirable step-fact premise; and P5 derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise. grounding.quote:
This family (F13 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides which record carries a piece of work, what that record may claim
and when the work closes. Its instance premises, which the commitments do
not supply, are named in the rows as follows: lifetimes, work and its
obligations last one run, one bounded batch or longer; several surfaces,
goals, tickets, comments, boards and summaries can each appear to state
the same work state; several tenants, one work item may be realised in
more than one build tenant; migrations, some work replaces one
authoritative truth path with another across producers, consumers and
proofs; carriers vary, a project may keep its carriers in files, trackers
or services. Each commitment's standing is written as the table of
commitments in FOUNDATIONS §3 states it.

An implementation migration ticket declares whether the active boundary is
rebuilding a pattern locally, consuming an existing reusable library or
commonisation surface, or extending that surface before the local

concepts.label: Library usage declaration

concepts.definition: Assessment distinct from construction output and from the decision owner's acceptance disposition. The reviewer is not the reviewed subject's author. grounding.quote:
The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
output and the independent-assessment protocol is
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse

concepts.label: Independent assessment

concepts.definition: Distinct reusable records of residual judgment J and owner ruling O, supported by computed facts C as applicable. J records a question, exact subject/basis, facts/evidence, actor/authority, conclusion/scope, uncertainty and concrete revising observation. O records original wording, owner, exact subject/basis, permitted scope/effects, conditions and source separately from agent interpretation. Repricing dispositions retained, superseded, deferred and withdrawn are owner-set obligation states, not core results, candidate acceptance or predecessor-claim qualification.

grounding.quote:
A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5. The record
identifies the question; the exact subject and governing basis; the
supporting computed facts and evidence; the responsible actor and its
authority; the conclusion and its scope; the uncertainty; and a concrete
revising observation that lets a consumer determine whether the conclusion
still applies.

concepts.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

concepts.definition: A bounded work claim whose completion is evaluated over every applicable declared obligation, exact subject/basis/scope, applicable judgments and rulings, and active non-closure conditions. The source identifies this condition with FOUNDATIONS §4 conjunction of results and makes this section its owner; SPEC_METHOD's consistency gate applies it over a change span.

grounding.quote:
A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
reserved acceptance

dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections

matters now. SPEC_METHOD: what constitutional change class and re-entry

exist and what state they are in. Comments: what was proposed, argued,
decided, reviewed or handed off. POSTING_GUIDE: how comment-layer
publications are structured and named.

conditions: A sprint enters close review.
exceptions: Local paydown debt may survive only where the governing method allows explicit follow-up.

grounding.quote:
Sprint close begins by moving the manifest to `status: closing`. While
closing: new iteration inside that sprint is frozen; every included ticket
or iteration entry is reviewed against the manifest; accumulated evidence
is checked for durability; changed surfaces are walked against cited
authority; deferred compliance is classified; paydown tickets are opened
where debt must survive past the close review (P6, P4b; rc.2
#sprint-close-review).

constraints.statement: Begin by setting the manifest to closing and freeze new iterations. Review every included ticket or iteration entry against the manifest; check evidence durability; walk changed surfaces against cited authority; classify deferred compliance; and open paydown tickets for surviving debt. Every reviewed item takes one of the six classifications under sprint authority, consuming but remaining separate from assessment results and taking exactly one core value for its acceptance predicate. Closed requires an outcome for every item and every debt entry and durable resulting paydown/repricing work; it does not require every outcome to be satisfied. Hidden authority drift cannot be accepted. The mappings add neither a disposition nor a core value, and consumers cannot treat remaining debt, repricing or removal as compliance.

grounding.quote:
A repository or external tracker carrier is lawful only
when it preserves the required ticket contract, history, state transition,
stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal
local copy (P3, P4b; rc.2 #one-durable-record-per-ticket). For a local
file, the filename should carry a stable id and a short slug. Recommended
local-file naming:
`T-001-add-product-layer.md`, `B-002-fix-reset-manifest-id.md`,
`S-003-evaluate-integration-capability.md`,
`C-004-clean-up-trace-tags.md`.

constraints.statement: Every ticket has exactly one durable authoritative record. A repository or external tracker is lawful only if it preserves required contract, history, state transition, stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal local copy. A local filename should contain a stable id and short slug; the T-001, B-002, S-003 and C-004 filenames are recommendations, not mandatory patterns.

conditions: The same admitted work genuinely has more than one tenant execution line.
The rule applies to backlog and active tickets.
exceptions: Completed tickets are not retroactively governed unless reopened or explicitly repriced.
A product definition may bind a path, display alias or tracker label as tenant identity.

grounding.quote:
The rule governs backlog and active tickets; it is not
retroactive for completed tickets unless a completed ticket is reopened or
explicitly repriced. It does not make every ticket multi-tenant: tenant
duplication is used only when the same admitted work item genuinely has
more than one tenant execution line (P3).

constraints.statement: Retain the upstream source/product/design ticket as its own authority surface and create one tenant-local ticket per build tenant, appending a tenant mnemonic to base id and filename. Status, proof, closure, repricing and reopening remain independent; one ticket cannot close more than one tenant lifecycle, and another tenant's green status cannot hide a blocker or false closure. Existing tenant duplicates should record source_ticket and build_tenant; build_tenant identifies the product's how.build_tenants entry, not an unbound alias. The unsuffixed base may remain upstream authority. Upstream-only and single-tenant work require no sibling duplication. This clause owns work-item/lifecycle relations in the consumed context, not tenant identity or realisation meaning.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket records at least `id`, `title`, `type`, `ticket_category`,
`status`, `goal`, `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`,
`triaged_at`, `created_at` and `updated_at` (P4b, P3; rc.2
#required-fields). Recommended additional fields: `priority`,
`dependencies`, `links`, `intake_source`, `affected_boundary`,
`source_ticket` when the ticket duplicates or derives from another ticket,
and `build_tenant` when the ticket is tenant-local.

For `ticket_category: implementation_migration` the ticket also carries
`migration_strategy` and `library_usage`; `governing_library` when
`library_usage` is `consume` or `extend`; and `library_rationale` when
`library_usage` is `none` (§6). A tenant-local implementation migration
also carries `build_tenant`, and `source_ticket` when it duplicates or
derives from an upstream source, product or design ticket.

For execution-contract admission the runtime-drafted contract should also
carry, at minimum, `target_truth`, `superseded_truth` when relevant,
`closure_law`, `evaluation_criteria`, `non_closure_conditions` and
`proof_surface` (§5).

constraints.statement: Every ticket records at least id, title, type, ticket_category, status, goal, change_intent, change_class, re_entry_point, triaged_at, created_at and updated_at. Priority, dependencies, links, intake_source and affected_boundary are recommended; source_ticket is recommended for derivation/duplication and build_tenant for tenant-local work. Migration tickets additionally require migration_strategy and library_usage, governing_library for consume/extend, and library_rationale for none. Tenant-local migrations require build_tenant and, when derived or duplicated upstream, source_ticket. A runtime-drafted admission contract should also carry target_truth, relevant superseded_truth, closure_law, evaluation_criteria, non_closure_conditions and proof_surface.

conditions: An implementation-migration wave has source-carrier and downstream-consumer tickets.
exceptions: Exploratory downstream work may proceed while the source ticket is active, but is non-closure evidence until the source carrier is admitted and authoritative.

grounding.quote:
Tickets that harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review
surfaces or other downstream consumers depend on those upstream source
tickets. A downstream ticket may carry exploratory work while the source
ticket is active, but that work is non-closure evidence until the source
carrier is admitted and authoritative. A downstream ticket does not close
while its upstream source-carrier ticket remains open. When one migration
wave introduces a new source carrier and then its prompt, projection or
read-model consumers, the dependency chain runs `source carrier ->
downstream consumers`, never the reverse.

constraints.statement: Sequencing follows SPEC_METHOD §7 inside-out law. Publishing/admitting the authoritative source carrier is upstream of prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review surfaces and other consumers. The dependency is source carrier → downstream consumers, never reversed; a downstream ticket cannot close while its upstream source-carrier ticket remains open.

grounding.quote:
Ticket category and change class are also orthogonal: `change_class`
governs lawful constitutional re-entry; `ticket_category` governs ticket
execution and closure discipline. A ticket may therefore be `type: bug`,
`ticket_category: implementation_migration`, `change_class: design_reframe`
without contradiction (P3).

constraints.statement: Record the class intake triage declared. Type, category and change class answer distinct questions; common pairings do not constrain the combinations to a closed matrix. A spike still records its current class and should end in a more specific downstream ticket or an explicit decision that no further substantive change is needed. Bug + implementation_migration + design_reframe is explicitly consistent.

conditions: Triage classifies work; the upward-walk refinement applies to bugs.

grounding.quote:
Before declaring `realization_refactor` for a bug, establish that the
current requirement and the accepted realising design govern the affected
behaviour and remain sufficient for the authorised outcome. Their presence
proves no coverage. Missing or ambiguous evidence leaves the affected
treatment unknown; it is not proof that the governing layer itself is
absent (P6).

Unresolved meaning remains J and a reserved choice remains O, as that
paragraph states (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Consume SPEC_METHOD §4's exact computed classification and residuals for declared owner/layer traversal, complete relevant public membership/value delta, accepted-design scope/trace coverage and rule-determined treatment; a new role does not repeat an unchanged walk. Before realization_refactor, establish that current requirement and accepted design govern the behavior and suffice. Presence alone proves no coverage; missing/ambiguous evidence leaves treatment unknown, not the governing layer absent. A public violation does not select a new contract; re-enter the governing owner only for explicitly changed desired outcome or established governing insufficiency. Walk upward from the realised surface, check each layer and stop at the highest missing/insufficient layer: missing/insufficient requirement → requirement_reprice and its owner; sufficient requirement but missing/insufficient design → design_reframe and Design; actual Goal/Intent/Product change → corresponding reprice and owner; sufficient requirement/design with implementation deviation → realization_refactor and repair or reject candidate. Use the smallest lawful re-entry exposed by the referenced rule; unresolved meaning remains J and reserved choice O.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced computed procedure is not supplied; its exact additional mechanics are unresolved.

conditions: The ticket is for substantive work.

grounding.quote:
a
ticket for substantive work carries the minimum metadata required by the
intake triage of [SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#universal-intake-triage):
the declared `change_intent`, the lawful `change_class`, the lawful
`re_entry_point`, and when triage occurred in `triaged_at` (P4b, P2; rc.2
#triage-metadata). The recorded values are those intake triage declared
(Change class and Upward propagation check above).

constraints.statement: As the durable work-tracking authority surface, a substantive-work ticket carries change_intent, lawful change_class, lawful re_entry_point and triaged_at with the values actually declared by intake triage.

grounding.quote:
An evaluation that reads a
declared state returns its own core value with its predicate under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Purpose and material
relation: a declared state is never combined as an evaluation result, so
a ticket marked `completed`, or a sprint marked `closed`, cannot stand in
for a `satisfied` result (P5, P1).

constraints.statement: Declared carrier states map to no core value and cannot be combined as evaluation results. An evaluation reading a state returns its own predicate-bound core value. Completed and closed therefore do not establish satisfied. Close classifications and debt-entry outcomes remain results with their separately specified mappings.

grounding.quote:
Backlog tickets live at the product definition's
`ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog` binding, by default
`.ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/`; active tickets at
`ticketing.tickets.lanes.active`, by default `.ai-workspace/tickets/active/`;
completed tickets move to `ticketing.tickets.lanes.completed`, by default
`.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/`

constraints.statement: Use product-definition ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed bindings; defaults are .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/, active/ and completed/. Completed tickets move to the completed binding. The separation keeps live execution bounded and searchable without forcing deferred work into comments or goals.

conditions: A derived surface or projected frame is insufficient for a named unresolved lifecycle or proof question.

grounding.quote:
If a derived surface or projected frame of this member is insufficient,
the actor reads this member only for the named unresolved lifecycle or
proof question and cites the clauses used (P2, P6; provenance rc.2
authority_compressions/ticket_method.compressed.md, a claim no rc.2 body
states; prompt construction is
[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)).

constraints.statement: The source prescribes reading this member only for that unresolved question and citing the clauses used; prompt construction belongs to ACTIVATION §2. The stated provenance is a compression claim not stated by an rc.2 body.
constraints.uncertainty: This is interpreted workflow data, not an instruction executed here.

conditions: The relevant lifetime, multi-surface, multi-tenant, migration or carrier-variation premise applies.

grounding.quote:
The table accounts for §1 to §9, and for POSTING_GUIDE §2, §7 and §9,
which have no family table of their own. §10 records dispositions and
decides nothing.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Record obligations before return on carriers covering their lifetime; create durable tickets only for surviving state under ticket-state authority. Presence/prose/lane/status admits neither contract nor growth basis. Execution and closure bind the same admitted basis. A sprint batches repeated closure law but never triage; it defers only declared local proof as escrow and law-changing work leaves for its own re-entry layer. A milestone establishes only its own claim; comments are provisional posts until adopted into the owning surface and retain their own discussion state. Rebinding leaves no rival authority. Migration closure needs negative or structural proof that the old scoped truth path no longer holds authority; similarity does not establish reusable identity or license automatic merging. Authoring authority is not independent verification; judgments/rulings remain bounded and durably reusable until affected by change. Every applicable closure obligation requires valid evidence; review occurrence does not close work and tests derive expectations from admitted authority. Unresolved material terms block affected admission/closure. Consumers apply these rules without new decisions: carrier selection consumers select whereas product bindings only locate; sprint consumers reuse these mappings rather than remap; term-binding and shape/reading rows have no separate consumer. The table claims coverage of §§1–9 and POSTING_GUIDE §§2,7,9, while §10 decides nothing.
constraints.uncertainty: External consumer loci and premise derivations are source assertions, not independently established in this interpretation.

conditions: Select the first matching case after establishing applicable upstream work authority; the local boundary is an admitted sprint, otherwise the current run.

grounding.quote:
| no applicable upstream work authority exists | no execution contract is admitted | do not create a ticket as substitute authority; stop or re-enter |
| applicable authority exists and an existing admitted ticket covers the exact work | derive the run-scoped contract from that ticket | reuse it; do not create another ticket |
| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work or an open obligation needs independent state beyond the local carrier boundary | one durable ticket plus the run-scoped contract | create or update the ticket only under ticket-state authority |
| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work stays inside one admitted sprint with no state required after sprint close | the sprint manifest plus one manifest-local iteration entry | do not create a durable ticket |
| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket or sprint covers the work, and the work ends in the current run with no independent surviving state | an intake-drafted run-scoped contract | do not create a durable ticket |

constraints.statement: No upstream authority: admit no contract, create no substitute-authority ticket, and stop or re-enter. Exact admitted ticket: derive the run contract and reuse that ticket without another. No exact ticket and state must survive the local boundary: use one durable ticket plus run contract, creating/updating only under ticket-state authority. No exact ticket and work stays in one admitted sprint with no post-close state: use manifest plus one manifest-local iteration entry, without durable ticket. No exact ticket or sprint and no independently surviving run state: use an intake-drafted run contract without durable ticket. Ticket absence neither requires nor authorises creation. An exact product-authorised instruction may supply one-run authority; generic requests and model-widened scope cannot. An explicit ticket-state-authority instruction selects durability, not contract admission or wider upstream authority.

grounding.quote:
When admission is absent or rejected, ACTIVATION §1 returns the missing
work authority without execution. Before that return, an obligation that
must survive the run is carried as follows (P4b, P6): it becomes a
sprint-local entry when its lifetime stays inside the admitted sprint;
otherwise it is recorded as a durable ticket, only under ticket-state
authority; where that authority is absent, it is retained in the
contract's named durable result and evidence surface or in an
already-authorised enclosing carrier, closure is marked withheld on
ticket-state authority, and the required re-entry is returned.

constraints.statement: ACTIVATION §1 owns invocation drafting/admission separation, execution-start conditions, admission coordinates, recording every result/withheld closure/residual before return, and refusal without a durable result/evidence surface. Product definition binds admission mechanism and that surface; if it is a ticket or manifest, record the admitted result and coordinates there. Lane, status or admission-asserting prose without coordinates is not admission evidence; the contract remains drafted or rejected. Absent/rejected admission returns missing authority without execution. Before return retain surviving obligations first as sprint-local entries when their lifetime fits an admitted sprint; otherwise as durable tickets under ticket-state authority; absent that authority use the named durable result/evidence surface or already-authorised enclosing carrier, mark closure withheld on ticket-state authority and return re-entry. Execution and closure use identical admitted categorisation, criteria, proof surface and non-closure conditions; resulting state still undergoes proof, gap analysis and repricing.
constraints.uncertainty: The exact admission-coordinate schema and step-side protocol are referenced but not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome,
prerequisite or experiment basis and does not admit that basis (ACTIVATION
§1). Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning the
selected goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy, and stays
durably legible in the existing goals or ticket authority
([SPEC_METHOD §3](SPEC_METHOD.md#3-outcome-conservation)). A ticket's
`active` status, its lane, or an admitted or retained contract is therefore
never the admission of a growth basis (P6, P2).

constraints.statement: Runtime flow should treat a ticket, sprint entry or draft contract as an admission candidate, never automatic truth. An admitted contract should be logged in runtime/event truth and available to prompt assembly and closure checking. Self-certification refusal belongs to ACTIVATION §1. Contract admission validates against cited product outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis without admitting that basis. Admission/renewal of the basis belongs to the selected goals-wave owner or explicitly bounded proxy and remains durable in goals/ticket authority. Active status, lane placement and admitted/retained contracts never admit a growth basis.

exceptions: Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by itself a non-closure condition; deferral requires SPEC_METHOD §7 path-relative authority and explicit disposition.

grounding.quote:
Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by
itself a non-closure condition. It may be deferred only under the
path-relative authority and explicit disposition rules of
[SPEC_METHOD §7](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-migration-options) (P2).

constraints.statement: A contract should expose progress/completion criteria and remaining failure conditions despite locally green proof; evaluation_criteria and non_closure_conditions should be visible as its local gain function. Typical migration non-closure conditions are an old authoritative path passing normal execution in affected scope; acceptance of mixed old/new proof; proxy/partial interfaces in the acceptance path; reachable competing/ambiguous executable authority on the claimed acceptance path; and unreconciled ticket/product/proof wording. These conditions are substantive execution safeguards, not optional commentary.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced path-relative deferral rules are not supplied.

conditions: A ticket spans contexts or a material term has competing meanings.

grounding.quote:
When a ticket spans contexts, or a material term has competing meanings,
the ticket cites the applicable product-definition disambiguation or the
owner-authorised import, translation, equivalence or disambiguation
carrier; it may reference that relation rather than duplicate it. Ticket
prose, actor familiarity, a matching glossary heading, tenant placement or
comment context cannot select meaning or transfer authority (P1, P6).

An unresolved or multiply resolved material term blocks execution-contract
admission and closure for the affected claim. Opening or updating the
ticket records the pressure and does not cure it; resolution re-enters at
the authority that owns the missing context or semantic relation (P1, P5).

constraints.statement: Cite product-definition disambiguation or an owner-authorised import, translation, equivalence or disambiguation carrier. Prose, familiarity, glossary-label matching, tenant placement and comment context cannot choose meaning or transfer authority. Unresolved or multiply resolved material terms block affected contract admission and closure; opening/updating the ticket only records pressure. Re-enter the owner of the missing context or semantic relation.

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration
exceptions: If no excluded or disjoint scope exists, explicitly declaring its absence satisfies that checklist item; silence does not.

grounding.quote:
The declaration states: the migration strategy used for this work item; the
exact affected migration scope; every explicitly excluded or disjoint
product or compatibility scope with its deterministic routing relation; the
old truth path or superseded contract; the new truth path or authoritative
contract; the producer set for the old and the new path; the consumer set
for the old and the new path; every projection, report, status surface and
proof surface derived from that contract family; and the closure law for
the migration.

constraints.statement: Carry an explicit declaration and hard live-markdown Migration Checklist as ticket authority, not commentary. Declare strategy, exact affected scope, every excluded/disjoint product or compatibility scope with deterministic routing, old/new truth paths/contracts, old/new producer and consumer sets, every derived projection/report/status/proof surface, and closure law. The minimum checklist covers named scope and exclusions; explicit old/new truth; listed new producers/consumers and projection/read-model surfaces; removal/demotion of old authority within scope; rejection of mixed-state closure evidence; removal/repricing of mixed-behavior tests; recurrence review; library usage with governing library or rationale; one lifecycle per backlog/active tenant ticket with suffixed siblings where multi-tenant; and reconciliation of ticket/product/proof wording before closure. Required strategy values are inside_out_hard_break and fundamental_re_adoption; library values are none, consume and extend. Consume/extend name governing_library; none explains no applicable reusable surface, boundary specificity or lack of lawful recurrence/commonisation candidacy in library_rationale.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD §7 owns migration law beyond this supplied local enforcement surface.

exceptions: An old path within affected scope may remain only as explicitly declared and ticket-justified retained compatibility.
Deterministically routed non-overlapping product scope outside affected scope retains its own current authority.

grounding.quote:
Closure is blocked while the old authoritative interface still passes in
normal execution within the declared affected scope, unless the ticket
explicitly declares a retained compatibility feature. A deterministically
routed, non-overlapping product scope outside the declared affected scope
remains governed by its own current authority (P6, P3). Accordingly: the
old path may not remain silently authoritative within the affected scope;
mixed old and new green tests do not count as migration completion; any
retained old path within the affected scope is named as compatibility
rather than current native truth; retained compatibility is justified in
the ticket itself, never inferred from surviving code; proxy or partial
implementations do not satisfy migration closure; and if a ticket was
marked `completed` and later review shows checked closure items are false
on the current tree, the ticket is reopened or an explicitly linked
successor ticket is created, because a false closure claim is a
ticket-method defect, not only a code defect (P6, P4b).

constraints.statement: Block closure while the old authoritative interface passes normal execution in affected scope, subject to the retained-compatibility exception. Compatibility is not current native truth and cannot be inferred from surviving code. Mixed old/new green tests and proxy/partial implementations do not establish completion. If current-tree review falsifies checked closure items of a completed ticket, reopen it or create an explicitly linked successor; false closure is also a ticket-method defect. An intermediate product slice may be accepted under SPEC_METHOD §7 path-relative promotion, whose slice derivation and acceptance criteria cannot be narrowed away by ticket wording. The migration ticket remains active until its checklist and final closure law are satisfied; active status renews no exhausted slice growth authority. Removal/demotion/closure-proof work may continue only within the referenced bound; further material producer/consumer growth needs another basis admitted under SPEC_METHOD §3.
constraints.uncertainty: The path-relative slice rule and continuation bound are external dependencies.

grounding.quote:
When `migration_strategy: fundamental_re_adoption`, the ticket carries the
explicit selection of fundamental re-adoption by the human product
authority; the comparison with bounded evolution across product value,
feedback latency, authority risk, reversibility, total cost and retained
predecessor semantics; the bounded abort or re-entry condition; the
sideways reference line or prior implementation boundary treated as source
material; the module and interface adjudication surface; and explicit
classifications for inherited modules, interfaces, carriers, projections
and proof surfaces, each `carry_across`, `redundant` or `rewrite`
([SPEC_METHOD §7](SPEC_METHOD.md#fundamental-migration) defines the three).
Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Inside_out_hard_break requires a full best-guess migrating-interface inventory, deepest-source-outward ordered break sequence, old seam intentionally severed by each break and expected negative proof for each. Fundamental_re_adoption requires explicit human product-authority selection; comparison against bounded evolution over product value, feedback latency, authority risk, reversibility, total cost and retained predecessor semantics; bounded abort/re-entry condition; sideways reference/prior implementation boundary as source material; module/interface adjudication surface; and classification of every inherited module/interface/carrier/projection/proof surface as carry_across, redundant or rewrite. Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The three inherited-implementation class definitions reside in unsupplied SPEC_METHOD §7.

conditions: Every implementation migration ticket, regardless of adopted Product profiles.
exceptions: When two boundaries or tickets already contain the same pattern, a third local rebuild is allowed only with consume, extend or an explicit linked do-not-commonise design decision in library_rationale.
Outside recurrence thresholds and applicable hard stops, a discovered reusable pattern does not block the bounded claim or require follow-up unless its owner admits that follow-up.

grounding.quote:
The recurrence rule is ticket law for every implementation migration
ticket, whichever profiles the Product adopts (P2, P4a): the second
credible recurrence forces an explicit
library or commonisation review; the third local rebuild is not acceptable
by default. If review shows the same realisation pattern already exists in
two module boundaries or tickets, a third local rebuild blocks
implementation unless the ticket declares `library_usage: consume`,
declares `library_usage: extend`, or links an explicit do-not-commonise
design decision in `library_rationale`. The preferred order is
boundary-local cleanup, then a tenant-local reusable library or
commonisation surface, then shared or common propagation only through
separate design re-entry (P2, P3). A Product that adopts DESIGN_MODULE
also applies its refinement,
[§10 Recurrence extraction](DESIGN_MODULE.md#recurrence-extraction),
which makes the same rule a design-review obligation and states what
counts as a commonisation candidate; it adds no rival threshold.

constraints.statement: The second credible recurrence requires explicit library/commonisation review; a third local rebuild is not acceptable by default and blocks implementation under the stated two-existing-boundaries condition unless an exception applies. Prefer boundary-local cleanup, then tenant-local reuse, then shared propagation only through separate design re-entry. Adopting DESIGN_MODULE adds its §10 design-review/candidate refinement without a rival threshold. Discoveries during active work remain subject to these rules; otherwise they are bounded repricing input.
constraints.uncertainty: The external refinement of commonisation candidacy is not supplied.

conditions: The same work item is processed across several build tenants; review concerns backlog and active tickets.
exceptions: Reopening, repricing or successor work may require upstream change when the source/product/design authority ticket itself must change.

grounding.quote:
When the same work item is processed across several build tenants, review
of backlog and active tickets checks that each tenant has its own suffixed
ticket; each ticket names its `build_tenant`; each tenant ticket has its
own proof surface and closure law; one tenant's green proof does not stand
in for another tenant's closure; and reopening, repricing and successor
work remain tenant-local unless the upstream source, product or design
ticket itself must change (P3, P6; rc.2 #multi-build-tenant-review-rule;
§4, Multi-build-tenant independence).

constraints.statement: Review checks a suffixed ticket and named build_tenant for each tenant, independent proof surface and closure law, no substitution of another tenant's green proof, and tenant-local reopening/repricing/successor work except for necessary upstream authority changes.

conditions: For a core-interface or carrier migration, a ticket-specific Functional Review Criteria section is recommended.

grounding.quote:
An implementation migration ticket makes the review problem concrete enough
that an implementor cannot land a rename, adapter, wrapper or happy-path
proof and claim source-truth migration (P6, P1; rc.2
#implementation-migration-review-disambiguation). For a core-interface or
carrier migration the ticket should include a `Functional Review Criteria`
section, specific to the ticket, such that a reviewer should be able to
answer these generic questions:

constraints.statement: Make review concrete enough to exclude rename/adapter/wrapper/happy-path substitution for source-truth migration. Recommended criteria let reviewers answer whether control-flow-owned meaning became admitted carrier/algebra/event/source truth; a semantic centre was removed rather than relocated; law is typed/closed rather than open dict/string/config; the main step is a pure transform rather than procedural law-deciding orchestration; effects are at publication/emission/delivery edges; consumers read admitted carriers rather than reconstruct from payloads, .get, defaults, raw text or legacy files; projections derive from source/events rather than close as rival authority; existing deterministic checks inform state without structurally blocking a constructive/probabilistic path permitted by the contract; and existing recurrence is consumed/extended rather than rebuilt. Passing tests alone do not satisfy review. Preserving the old semantic centre through typed wrappers, adapter policy, old lists beside algebra, fallback config or rehydrated dictionaries fails despite green public behavior.

conditions: A migration concerns a core interface, carrier or authoritative contract.
exceptions: Compatibility shims may satisfy the checklist only if explicitly justified as retained compatibility.

grounding.quote:
For a core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration, the
ticket includes an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be
used as closure evidence. The checklist is a named walk of every live
interface that can still bypass, reinterpret, replay or project the
migrating truth path

constraints.statement: Include an Impacted Interface Review Checklist before using tests as closure evidence, naming every live bypass/reinterpretation/replay/projection interface. It should enumerate existing source builders; closure/register/projection builders; deepest kernel and adapters; public wrappers and bootstrap/replay/ingest/resume/query entrypoints; prompt/report/projection/read-model surfaces; constructors/materialisation; proof lanes and negative fixtures. Each item states interface-specific closure, such as consuming admitted projections without raw helper authority, exposing read models without silent reconstruction, or preventing open payload aggregation from becoming independent closure. A checked box asserts current-tree truth; a false checked item makes the ticket not closure-ready. Deferred interfaces name a successor or stay unchecked. Hard-break checklists describe seam inventory before test evidence; re-adoption checklists cover inherited modules/interfaces carried, dropped or rewritten, without implicit carry-forward.

conditions: A migration ticket touches a core interface.
constraints.statement: Include Required Break Order or an equivalent ordered section: discover the full best-guess interface family; publish/admit new source carrier; sever one old authoritative seam and keep it broken; rebind deepest kernel; remove/demote old producers; rebind old consumers; then reprice projections/reports/prompts/delivery/tests. Several old interfaces additionally require a Break-To-Closure Map linking each break to its closure-law clause. Review treats as defects old authority inside typed wrappers, new carriers beside old authoritative read models, proxies keeping old interfaces under new names, constructor/replay/ingest/resume/bootstrap/wrapper admission bypasses, projections/tests passing without new carriers, fallbacks inventing policy/identity/target/closure truth, and downstream proof passing while source work remains open.

exceptions: An old affected-scope or acceptance-path route may remain only if explicitly specified as retained compatibility.
A deterministically routed non-overlapping outside scope does not block this migration merely because its independently governed path works.

grounding.quote:
For a migration ticket, positive behaviour proof is not enough. The proof
surface should include at least one negative or structural proof that
the old path can no longer satisfy the closure law (P6, P5; rc.2
#mixed-state-negative-proof).

For a ticket with an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist`, the negative
proof exercises the named public consumers that matter for closure. Proving
that one legacy shim is bypassed is not sufficient when the live authority
path already bypasses that shim through other helpers, loaders or rebuild
paths (P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: Positive behavior proof is insufficient; the proof surface should include at least one negative/structural proof that the old path cannot satisfy closure law. Examples are rejecting the severed seam before accepting downstream repair as progress; failing closed if the new carrier is removed; rejecting legacy payloads without admitted carriers; resolving deliberately conflicting old/new fixtures in favor of new truth or failing closed; rejecting structurally different same-name carriers/functions/routes/policies/projections; and avoiding undeclared local fixtures or mutable sibling workspaces in required closure proof. Keep the ticket open if the old path normally works in scope or remains reachable on the claimed acceptance path, subject to explicit exceptions. Where an interface checklist exists, negative proof must exercise named public consumers relevant to closure; bypassing one legacy shim is insufficient if helpers/loaders/rebuild paths already bypass it.

conditions: Independent assessment is required at product, qualification, release and explicitly risk-bearing boundaries that claim it, or additional boundaries imposed by a governing basis.
exceptions: It is not required for every local implementation step.

grounding.quote:
Independent review is required at
product, qualification, release and explicitly risk-bearing boundaries that
claim it, not for every local implementation step (P6, P2).

A claimed independent review may support promotion or closure only when its
exact subject and verdict are durably traceable through an existing ticket,
commentary, qualification or release-evidence carrier. A statement that
review occurred, an unbound conversation summary or an unavailable draft is
not the review verdict. This rule requires no separate receipt, carrier or
review round (P6, P4b).

constraints.statement: Author/implementer authority does not confer independent verification. Identify exact subject, basis, scope, exclusions, evidence, verdict and unresolved findings, and cite current authority plus code/proof paths rather than historical commentary alone. Self-review remains authoring evidence; neither relabeling nor human acceptance/rejection makes it independent. Promotion/closure support requires durable traceability of exact subject and verdict through an existing ticket/commentary/qualification/release-evidence carrier; occurrence assertions, unbound summaries and unavailable drafts are not verdicts. No separate receipt/carrier/round is required. Review is bounded by the exact claim and applicable hard stops; EVALUATION §5 alone supplies finding-blocking criteria and this member adds no trigger.
constraints.uncertainty: Full independence protocol and finding-blocking rules are referenced externally.

grounding.quote:
Where the agentic construction relation applies (ACTIVATION §1, bound to
this method by [SPEC_METHOD §8](SPEC_METHOD.md#8-bounded-execution-in-this-method)),
the active work item identifies the selected execution basis, the bounded
affected relation set, the delegated construction and assessment authority,
and the re-entry conditions. It may point to accepted design and existing
evidence carriers rather than restate them. Ticket state, ticket prose or
an admitted execution contract cannot widen that basis or substitute for
the live-surface assessment the relation requires (P6, P0).

constraints.statement: A direct or lawfully proxied human ruling receives durable disposition before the next affected acceptance boundary, with source wording distinct from interpretation; ticket creation neither satisfies the obligation nor permits widening. Where the agentic construction relation applies, the work item identifies selected basis, bounded affected relations, delegated construction/assessment authority and re-entry conditions; references to accepted design/evidence may replace restatement. Ticket state/prose/admitted contract cannot widen basis or replace required live-surface assessment. Existing ticket/commentary/commit/qualification/release-evidence can carry the reviewable transition; no new state, document type, review round or approval ceremony is required. This member carries selection/traceability; ACTIVATION §1 and SPEC_METHOD §8 own execution semantics.

exceptions: Questions settled by rule require no invented J record.
A new role or conversation alone invalidates nothing.

grounding.quote:
Later roles and resumed runs recover the result and check its
applicability rather than re-author unchanged judgment. Reuse and
invalidation are
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse): changed material
inputs, a declared revising observation or a changed basis invalidate
the affected result, preserving the original result and its successor
relation and keeping only demonstrably independent results, and a new
role or conversation alone invalidates nothing. For a recorded judgment
the material inputs include its supporting computed facts and evidence,
and its declared revising observation is the one the record states;
reassessment covers what the change affects. The result may reference
current C outputs; reuse cannot silently turn unknown facts into
established premises (P4b, P5). Required independent assessment may consume valid C, but
its assessor acquires sufficient exact evidence and supplies its own
judgment under the actual independence condition; reusing the author's J
cannot satisfy that condition (P6; EVALUATION §3).

constraints.statement: Record a residual judgment needed by another activation once with owning work in its selected existing carrier. Later roles recover and check applicability rather than re-author unchanged judgment. Changed material inputs, supporting computed facts/evidence, declared revising observation or basis invalidate affected results; preserve original and successor relation and only demonstrably independent results, reassessing affected scope.
